stem: Rate of GST on essential commodities is ____.
solution: Essential commodities are exempt from GST, so the rate of GST on them is \(0\%\). Correct option: C.

stem: Out of the following equations which one is not a quadratic equation?
solution: In (A), \(x^2 + 4x = 11 + x^2\) reduces to \(4x - 11 = 0\), a linear equation (the \(x^2\) terms cancel), so it is not quadratic. (B) \(x^2 - 4x = 0\), (C) \(5x^2 - 90 = 0\) and (D) \(2x^2 - 2x + 5 = 0\) are all quadratic. Correct option: A.

stem: To draw graph of \(4x + 5y = 19\), find the value of \(y\) when \(x = 1\).
solution: Put \(x = 1\) in \(4x + 5y = 19\): \(4 + 5y = 19\), so \(5y = 15\) and \(y = 3\). Correct option: B.

subtopic: Sum of n Terms of an A.P.
stem: Sum of first five multiples of 3 is ____.
solution: First five multiples of 3 are \(3, 6, 9, 12, 15\). Their sum \(= 3 + 6 + 9 + 12 + 15 = 45\). Correct option: A.

stem: On certain article if rate of CGST is \(9\%\), then what is the rate of GST?
solution: GST is shared equally as CGST and SGST, so rate of SGST \(= 9\%\) as well. Rate of GST \(=\) rate of CGST \(+\) rate of SGST \(= 9\% + 9\% = 18\%\).

stem: For simultaneous equations in variables \(x\) and \(y\), if \(D_x = -42\) and \(D = -3\), then find the value of \(x\).
solution: By Cramer's Rule, \(x = \dfrac{D_x}{D} = \dfrac{-42}{-3} = 14\).

stem: When two coins are tossed simultaneously, write the sample space \(S\).
solution: Each coin can show Head (H) or Tail (T). Sample space \(S = \{HH, HT, TH, TT\}\), so \(n(S) = 4\).

stem: Write the following quadratic equation in the form \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\): \(2y = 10 - y^2\).
solution: \(2y = 10 - y^2\). Bring all terms to one side: \(y^2 + 2y - 10 = 0\). This is in the form \(ay^2 + by + c = 0\) with \(a = 1,\ b = 2,\ c = -10\).

stem: If one die is rolled, then complete the activity to find the probability of the event that the number on the upper face is prime.
solution: \(S\) is the sample space. \(S = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}\), so \(n(S) = 6\). Event A: prime number on the upper face, \(A = \{2, 3, 5\}\), so \(n(A) = 3\). \(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

If two coins are tossed simultaneously, find the probability of the event "getting at least one head."
solution: Sample space \(S = \{HH, HT, TH, TT\}\), so \(n(S) = 4\). Event A: at least one head, \(A = \{HH, HT, TH\}\), so \(n(A) = 3\). \(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{3}{4}\).

stem: Solve the following simultaneous equations: \(x + y = 4\); \(2x - y = 2\).
solution: Adding the two equations: \((x + y) + (2x - y) = 4 + 2\), so \(3x = 6\) and \(x = 2\). Substituting in \(x + y = 4\): \(2 + y = 4\), so \(y = 2\). Solution: \(x = 2,\ y = 2\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem: If \(\sum x_i f_i = 1265\) and \(N = 50\), then find the mean of the given data.
solution: Mean \(\bar{x} = \dfrac{\sum x_i f_i}{N} = \dfrac{1265}{50} = 25.3\).

stem: Shreekar bought a Laptop with \(10\%\) discount on printed price. The printed price of that Laptop was \(\text{₹}\,50{,}000\). \(18\%\) GST was charged on discounted price. Complete the activity to find the amount of CGST and SGST. What amount did Shreekar pay?
One of the roots of the quadratic equation \(5m^2 + 2m + k = 0\) is \(\dfrac{-7}{5}\). Complete the activity to find the value of \(k\).
solution: Since \(\dfrac{-7}{5}\) is a root, put \(m = \dfrac{-7}{5}\) in the equation: \(5\left(\dfrac{-7}{5}\right)^2 + 2\left(\dfrac{-7}{5}\right) + k = 0\). So \(5\times \dfrac{49}{25} - \dfrac{14}{5} + k = 0\), i.e. \(\dfrac{49}{5} - \dfrac{14}{5} + k = 0\), giving \(\dfrac{35}{5} + k = 0\), so \(7 + k = 0\) and \(k = -7\).

stem: Two numbers differ by 3. The sum of twice the smaller number and thrice the greater number is 19. Find the numbers.
solution: Let the greater number be \(x\) and the smaller be \(y\). Then \(x - y = 3\) and \(2y + 3x = 19\). From the first, \(x = y + 3\). Substitute: \(2y + 3(y + 3) = 19\), so \(5y + 9 = 19\), giving \(5y = 10\) and \(y = 2\). Then \(x = 5\). The numbers are 5 and 2.

stem: Sachin invested some amount in a National Saving Certificate Scheme. In the first year he invested \(\text{₹}\,5{,}000\), in the second year \(\text{₹}\,7{,}000\), in the third year \(\text{₹}\,9{,}000\) and so on. Find the total amount that he invested in 12 years.
solution: The yearly investments \(5000, 7000, 9000, \ldots\) form an A.P. with \(a = 5000,\ d = 2000,\ n = 12\). \(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}\left[2a + (n-1)d\right] = \dfrac{12}{2}\left[2\times 5000 + 11\times 2000\right] = 6\left[10000 + 22000\right] = 6\times 32000 = \text{₹}\,1{,}92{,}000\).

stem: There are six cards in a box, each bearing a number from 0 to 5. Find the probability of each of the following events, that: (1) The number on the card drawn is a natural number. (2) The number on the card drawn is a whole number.

Draw a histogram of the following data:

| Height of Students (cm) | No. of Students |
|---|---|
| 135–140 | 4 |
| 140–145 | 12 |
| 145–150 | 16 |
| 150–155 | 8 |
solution: Take the class-intervals of height (cm) on the X-axis and the number of students on the Y-axis (a continuous scale, since the classes are continuous). Draw adjacent rectangles (bars with no gaps) on each class-interval with heights equal to the frequencies: \(135\text{–}140\to 4\), \(140\text{–}145\to 12\), \(145\text{–}150\to 16\), \(150\text{–}155\to 8\). The resulting adjacent bars form the required histogram.

stem: The sum of two roots of a quadratic equation is 7 and sum of their cubes is 91, find the equation.
solution: Let the roots be \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Given \(\alpha + \beta = 7\) and \(\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = 91\). Using \(\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = (\alpha + \beta)^3 - 3\alpha\beta(\alpha + \beta)\): \(91 = 7^3 - 3\alpha\beta(7) = 343 - 21\alpha\beta\). So \(21\alpha\beta = 343 - 91 = 252\), giving \(\alpha\beta = 12\). The required equation is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\), i.e. \(x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0\).

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: Smt. Tejaswini purchased 100 shares of FV \(\text{₹}\,80\) when the MV is \(\text{₹}\,900\). She paid brokerage at the rate of \(0.5\%\) and \(18\%\) GST on brokerage. Find the following: (1) Net amount paid for 100 shares. (2) Brokerage paid on sum invested. (3) GST paid on brokerage. (4) Total amount paid for 100 shares.
solution: (1) Net amount (sum invested) for 100 shares \(= 100\times \text{MV} = 100\times 900 = \text{₹}\,90{,}000\). (2) Brokerage \(= 0.5\%\) of \(90{,}000 = \dfrac{0.5}{100}\times 90{,}000 = \text{₹}\,450\). (3) GST on brokerage \(= 18\%\) of \(450 = \dfrac{18}{100}\times 450 = \text{₹}\,81\). (4) Total amount paid \(= 90{,}000 + 450 + 81 = \text{₹}\,90{,}531\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
The following table shows the funds collected by 105 students for flood affected people. Find the median of the data.

| Fund (Rupees) | No. of Students |
|---|---|
| 10–20 | 10 |
| 20–30 | 37 |
| 30–40 | 15 |
| 40–50 | 20 |
| 50–60 | 7 |
| 60–70 | 8 |
| 70–80 | 8 |
solution: \(N = 105\), so \(\dfrac{N}{2} = 52.5\). Cumulative frequencies: \(10, 47, 62, 82, 89, 97, 105\). The cumulative frequency just exceeding \(52.5\) is \(62\), so the median class is \(30\text{–}40\). Here \(L = 30,\ cf = 47,\ f = 15,\ h = 10\). Median \(= L + \dfrac{\frac{N}{2} - cf}{f}\times h = 30 + \dfrac{52.5 - 47}{15}\times 10 = 30 + \dfrac{5.5\times 10}{15} = 30 + \dfrac{55}{15} = 30 + 3.67 \approx 33.67\). Median \(\approx \text{₹}\,33.67\).

stem:
A survey was conducted in the school. Student using different modes of transport is given below:

| Mode of Transport | Percentage of Students |
|---|---|
| Bicycle | 35 |
| Bus | \(a\) |
| Railway | \(2a\) |
| Rickshaw | 20 |

Find the value of \(a\) and draw the Pie diagram.
solution: The percentages total \(100\): \(35 + a + 2a + 20 = 100\), so \(3a + 55 = 100\), giving \(3a = 45\) and \(a = 15\). Hence Bus \(= 15\%\) and Railway \(= 2a = 30\%\). The measure of the central angle for each mode \(= \dfrac{\text{percentage}}{100}\times 360^\circ\): Bicycle \(= \dfrac{35}{100}\times 360^\circ = 126^\circ\); Bus \(= \dfrac{15}{100}\times 360^\circ = 54^\circ\); Railway \(= \dfrac{30}{100}\times 360^\circ = 108^\circ\); Rickshaw \(= \dfrac{20}{100}\times 360^\circ = 72^\circ\). Draw a circle and mark sectors of these central angles to obtain the required pie diagram.

stem: There are some students in group A and group B. If one student goes from group A to group B, then the number of students in both groups is same. But if one student goes from group B to group A, then the number of students in group A becomes twice of group B. Find the number of students in each group.
solution: Let group A have \(x\) students and group B have \(y\) students. If one goes A to B: \(x - 1 = y + 1\), so \(x - y = 2\) ... (i). If one goes B to A: \(x + 1 = 2(y - 1)\), so \(x + 1 = 2y - 2\), giving \(x - 2y = -3\) ... (ii). Subtract (ii) from (i): \((x - y) - (x - 2y) = 2 - (-3)\), so \(y = 5\). Then from (i), \(x = 7\). Group A has 7 students and group B has 5 students.
